runner.text:
**What these checks were looking at**

I was tracing how the plate‑loading tool (the one branded "plate‑pool") is wired into the athlete's published pages, to confirm the links are being generated consistently from the kit on file. Nothing here was a training command — no plan was drafted, no record written, no change proposed, and no warnings came back from anything run. This is purely a read of how things currently stand.

**Where the plate tool shows up**

The plate tool is referenced in five places: the coach settings, the profile, the home kit definition, the athlete summary page, and every published routine page. There are seven routine pages — Monday overhead press, Wednesday pull‑up, Friday squat, Saturday bench, Sunday deadlift, the conditioning circuit, and the daily hang — and each one carries a "Set up the home kit in plate‑pool" link on its seventh line, right under the heading. That link loads the full home inventory into the tool in one go, so the athlete only has to tap it once per device.

Below that, individual exercises carry a "Load it in plate‑pool" link that opens the tool pre‑set to a specific implement and load. The ones found across the pages are:

- Barbell at 140.5 lb, with collar clamps
- Barbell at 55.5 lb, with collar clamps
- Dumbbell at 32.5 lb, with standard screw collars
- Dumbbell at 5 lb, with no collar hardware
- Dumbbell at 20 lb, with standard screw collars (this one appears twice, on two different pages)
- Kettlebell at 40 lb, with standard screw collars

Every one of those links points at the same home kit, so what the tool shows will match whatever the athlete actually has on the floor.

**How the locations are configured**

The settings define two training locations. "Home" is a plate‑pool location using the kit named "home", and it maps five implement types: barbell, dumbbell, kettlebell, a leg attachment, and a weighted vest. "Gym" is a fixed‑increment ("grid") location mapping a bar, dumbbells, and kettlebells; the output cut off before showing the gym's increment and range figures, so I can't quote those yet. The athlete page states the same home mapping in its own words, so the two agree.

Two general figures also appeared in the settings: sessions are budgeted at 75 minutes, and check‑ins are on a 7‑day cadence.

**A sample page**

The Monday page is headed "Mon · OHP, back and arms," is marked as a home session, and is written for the week of 2026‑11‑02. Its first exercise is Overhead Press (Barbell), opening with a warm‑up single set of 5 at 33 lb, then a warm‑up single set of 3 at 48 lb. The page carries a note that it is generated from the store and that any hand edits will be overwritten the next time pages are published — so if something on a page looks wrong, the fix has to go through the engine, not the page itself.

**Housekeeping**

The pages folder is clean — nothing edited and unpublished — and the most recent commit touching the athlete page was a routine publish. The pages are pushed to the athlete's training repository on GitHub, and the plate tool itself is hosted on the same account's site, so the links will keep working as long as both stay published.

**What the athlete needs to do**

Nothing. There is no proposed change for them to agree to and no warning to clear. If anything, the useful takeaway for them is: tap the "Set up the home kit" link once on their phone, and after that the per‑exercise "Load it" links will show exactly which plates to put on for each prescribed load.

first.text:
Yes. The long link I pasted earlier is exactly that: it loads your whole home kit (barbell, dumbbells, kettlebell, leg attachment, weighted vest) into plate-pool in one tap, and you only need to do it once per device.

Where to find it on your phone: open any of your routine pages in the training repo (Monday overhead press, Wednesday pull-up, Friday squat, Saturday bench, Sunday deadlift, the conditioning circuit, or the daily hang) and it's the first link under the heading, labelled "Set up the home kit in plate-pool." It isn't on the athlete summary page, which is why you didn't see it there.

Once you've tapped it, the "Load it in plate-pool" links beside each exercise will open the tool already set to that day's bar or dumbbell load and show you which plates to put on.
